column1: # Authored source dependencies for the ECMA-262 census, in the URL lane's
# format: one line per row id, then a tab, then a comma-separated list of the
# identities that row consumes, or a bare `-` for none. Identity checks do not
# Every row of the census appears exactly once. Every target is either another
# row of this census or an `ext.` identity declared in externals.tsv; a
# duplicate or self dependency fails generation.
# Scope of a line. For a primary (clause) row the dependencies are read from
# the clause's OWN text — its span minus the spans of its clause children —
# because clause rows nest and the generator does not subtract child spans, so
# reading the whole span would make `clause.promise-objects` depend on
# everything under it. For a `field`, `slot`, `requirement` or `term` row the
# whole span is read. Operation names are matched on identifier boundaries, so
# `PromiseResolve` is not read out of `NewPromiseResolveThenableJob` and
# The four escape treatments are rulings R-P6, R-P9 and R-P11, and the
#   ext.ecma262.core.*         the named ES2026 core boundary: Completion
#                              creation, the object-model operations, and the
#                              List and Record specification types. R-P9: this
#                              fixes only WHERE an escaping reference is
#                              recorded, never a disposition. No in-scope row
#                              the completion discipline is reproduced by the
#   ext.ecma262.iterator.*     R-P11: the iterator tape the four combinators
#   ext.ecma262.intrinsic.*    R-P11: the well-known intrinsics and symbols.
#   ext.ecma262.conventions.*  R-P11: the conventions record — the enum
#                              spellings, the list notation, and annex D.
#   ext.ecma262.host.*         R-P6 externals: agents, realms, execution
#                              contexts, and Script and Module Records.
#   ext.ecma262.out-of-lane.*  R-P11: the two in-family hooks that were found
